first.rationale: Prior evidence indicates shorter onboarding durably improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption, directly addressing both current declines. Promotional pricing may counter the competitor in the short term, but its documented 30-day retention harm conflicts with the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Verify both records before committing to confirm effect scope and retention trade-offs.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and supports sustainable value: completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. Do not use promotional pricing despite competitor pressure: its verified revenue lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle. The remaining uncertainty is whether the prior onboarding effect replicates under current competitive conditions and whether it fully reverses the 6% activation decline; retain appropriate holdout measurement across completion, activation, qualified revenue, and retention.
